domains.name: Confounding
domains.direction_justification: In the matched cohort, personal history of breast cancer was 7.8% in controls vs 5.9% in the GLP-1 group (and 9.2% vs 5.9% in the full cohort). Higher baseline personal history increases subsequent event risk in the control group, artificially driving the odds ratio below 1.0 (OR 0.695).

findings.title: Unmatched baseline history of breast cancer
findings.mechanism: Control group had a 32% higher relative prevalence of prior breast cancer (7.8% vs 5.9% in matched cohort), directly inflating event rates in controls.
evidence: Matched cohort history of breast cancer: control 7.8% vs GLP-1 5.9%

findings.title: Severe unadjusted comorbidity imbalance and competing risk
findings.mechanism: GLP-1 users had nearly double the rate of severe comorbidity, predisposing them to competing mortality before breast cancer diagnosis.

domains.name: Measurement of the exposure
domains.direction_justification: Defining exposure as any single prior or current prescription without minimum duration, cumulative dose, or washout period, while requiring first prescription before cutoff, introduces immortal time bias and includes non-adherent patients as exposed, skewing results away from null.

findings.title: Crude exposure definition and immortal time bias
findings.mechanism: Patients with a single prescription are classified as exposed without verifying continuation or dose; observation window (2022-2025) is too short (3.5 years) for solid tumor biology without strict induction/lag windows.
evidence: Any prior or current GLP-1 prescription

domains.name: Selection of participants into the study
domains.direction_justification: Conditioning inclusion entirely on undergoing mammography (217,624 women screened) creates collider/selection bias, as screening behavior correlates with health-seeking status and socioeconomic factors.

findings.title: Restriction to mammography attendees
findings.mechanism: Selection filter requires prior mammogram, introducing selection bias regarding who gets screened and who is subsequently prescribed GLP-1.
evidence: Cohort restricted to women undergoing mammography (217,624 -> 111,646)

domains.name: Post-exposure interventions
domains.direction_justification: No data are provided on concomitant medications, weight loss interventions, or cancer preventive therapies during follow-up.

findings.title: Missing data on co-interventions
findings.mechanism: Cannot assess differential use of post-exposure treatments without pharmacological tracking.

domains.name: Missing data
domains.direction_justification: The passport contains no reporting on missing EHR records, variable completeness, or loss to follow-up.

findings.title: Absence of missingness reporting
findings.mechanism: Unknown extent of missing covariates or incomplete follow-up in EHR.

domains.name: Measurement of the outcome
domains.direction_justification: Screening frequency was explicitly not matched between groups, making it impossible to determine if breast cancer detection was systematically higher or lower in GLP-1 users.

findings.title: Unmatched screening frequency and surveillance bias
findings.mechanism: Differential routine mammogram adherence between groups can cause detection bias in either direction.
evidence: Matching NOT conducted on screening frequency

domains.name: Selection of the reported result
domains.direction_justification: Logistic regression without time-to-event modeling ignores censoring and competing mortality (Charlson >= 5 was 19.7% in GLP-1 vs 10.4% in controls), artificially decreasing observed GLP-1 odds (OR 0.695).

findings.title: Failure to perform time-to-event and competing risk analysis
findings.mechanism: Binary logistic regression treats all follow-up as static and ignores differential death/censoring risks in a heavily comorbid GLP-1 cohort.
evidence: Logistic regression used; time-to-event analysis not performed

overall.summary: The study exhibits a critical risk of bias driven by unadjusted baseline confounding (controls had significantly higher baseline breast cancer history, 7.8% vs 5.9% in matched cohort), immortal time bias from a permissive exposure definition, selection on mammography attendance, and failure to account for competing mortality in logistic regression despite GLP-1 patients having nearly double the rate of high comorbidity (19.7% vs 10.4% Charlson >= 5). These biases systematically push the effect estimate away from the null towards an apparent protective effect (matched OR 0.695).

unresolvable_without_more_data: Data on post-exposure co-interventions and adjuvant therapies across both arms.
Data on EHR completeness, missingness proportion, and patient loss to follow-up.
Exact mammography screening frequency per patient during follow-up to settle direction of surveillance bias.
Time-to-event data with competing risks of death (Fine-Gray / cause-specific hazards).

points.reason: The auditor accurately identified the unadjusted baseline history of breast cancer imbalance with exact numbers (7.8% vs 5.9% matched, 9.2% vs 5.9% full cohort) and correctly identified the direction of bias (higher risk in controls explaining the apparent protective effect).
points.quote: In the matched cohort, personal history of breast cancer was 7.8% in controls vs 5.9% in the GLP-1 group (and 9.2% vs 5.9% in the full cohort). Higher baseline personal history increases subsequent event risk in the control group, artificially driving the odds ratio below 1.0 (OR 0.695).

points.reason: The auditor correctly recognized that the GLP-1 cohort was significantly sicker across comorbidity indices (Charlson >=5 19.7% vs 10.4%, cardiac 13.0% vs 7.3%, renal 13.9% vs 7.1%) and avoided the healthy user effect trap, framing it as competing risk / selection against null.
points.quote: Charlson Index >= 5: GLP-1 19.7% vs control 10.4%; Cardiac disease: GLP-1 13.0% vs control 7.3%; Renal disease: GLP-1 13.9% vs control 7.1%

points.reason: The auditor explicitly identified the prevalent-user / crude exposure definition, lack of washout, lack of minimum duration, lack of dose tracking, immortal time bias, and the failure to use time-to-event analysis instead of binary logistic regression.
points.quote: Defining exposure as any single prior or current prescription without minimum duration, cumulative dose, or washout period... introduces immortal time bias... Binary logistic regression treats all follow-up as static and ignores differential death/censoring risks

points.reason: The auditor completely missed the issue regarding matching on maximum BMI rather than weight trajectory and the artificial enrichment of diabetes in the matched control group (53.4% vs 17.6%).
The auditor accurately calculated the absolute risk difference (ARR 0.69% / 2.31% to 1.62%) and NNT (~144).

extra_findings.title: Restriction to mammography attendees as collider/selection bias
extra_findings.why: Restricting the cohort strictly to women who underwent mammography introduces selection on health-seeking behavior and screening adherence.

extra_findings.title: Unmatched screening frequency during follow-up
extra_findings.why: Follow-up screening frequency was not matched, leaving potential for detection/surveillance bias.

verdict.notes: The auditor provided an exceptionally strong quantitative analysis, catching 4 out of 5 reference points with exact figures and avoiding all traps. It only omitted the specific critique of matching on maximum baseline BMI vs weight trajectory and diabetes comparator composition (P4).
